verdict: A near-faithful rebuild of the Wikipedia main page with every block, text and photo in place; the gaps are 1-3 px vertical drifts and lighter greys on borders, and it is a reasonably editable page with flowing columns and templated menus but an absolutely positioned header and few named groups.

top_defects.where: whole page, text lines and photos
top_defects.what: vertical drift of 1-3 CSS px: wordmark ~2 px higher than reference, 'Welcome to Wikipedia,' ~1-2 px lower, 'In the news' photo ~3 px higher and its bullet lines 1-2 px off; enough to light up the whole heatmap (bottom-right cells meanDiff 22-25)
search field border #a2a9b1 instead of #72777d (visibly lighter), welcome banner border #c8ccd1 instead of #dddddd, tab bar rule darker than reference
sections (featured article, Did you know, Help us improve, In the news) are loose h2 + paragraphs inside the column, not named section groups; only 14 of 130 layers named
menu icon, logo, search and user links each absolutely placed inside the header; tabs, main and aside also absolute on the frame rather than a page grid
the four section headings copy the same h2 classes (h-[37px], border colors, padding) by hand, link color #3366cc repeated ~60 times as an arbitrary value; 237 arbitrary values, no shared tokens
section headings and welcome title use #202122 instead of #101418, headings 19 px instead of 19.2 px; tiny line-height offsets in banner subtitle (22 px vs 24.7)

strengths: Every text of the reference present with identical wrapping, links, bold and italics, including the truncated 'Did you know' line and 'Anna Korwin-' cut at the bottom
Correct geometry of the banner and the two colored columns (#f5fffa / #f5faff, heading fills #cef2e0 / #cedff2 with their darker borders)
Appearance menu and user links / view tabs built as templates with data, radios drawn in HTML with the selected #3366cc state
